qdrant.title: Build RAG pipelines with Qdrant and Azure Files – Microsoft Learn
qdrant.notes: Qdrant is a vector database written in Rust that serves as the vector store for similarity search in a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline, with Azure Files as the document source. Orchestration frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex and Haystack handle ingestion and retrieval at query time. Qdrant can store arbitrary JSON-serializable metadata as a payload and filter on it when a query runs. According to the page, filtering happens during HNSW graph traversal instead of as a post-filter, so search performance is not reduced by the filter. Collections are created automatically on the first insert, with a fitting vector dimension and distance metric. It can be self-hosted, for example on Azure Kubernetes Service together with Azure Files private endpoints, which keeps the pipeline inside the tenant's network boundary. Alternatively, Qdrant Cloud offers a managed service with the same API as the self-hosted version, and a free tier suffices for development and testing. It is also available through the Azure Marketplace, which allows billing through an Azure subscription. The page does not state licensing terms, capacity limits or performance figures.

quick-access-toolbar.title: Customize the Quick Access Toolbar – Microsoft Support
quick-access-toolbar.notes: The Quick Access Toolbar is a customizable toolbar holding commands that stay available regardless of which ribbon tab is currently shown. By default it sits above the ribbon in the title bar, and it can be moved below the ribbon. Users show or hide it through the right-click menu on the ribbon. Command labels can only be displayed when the toolbar is placed below the ribbon. Commands are added by right-clicking a ribbon command or by choosing More Commands for items that are not on the ribbon, and they can be removed or reordered in the options dialog under File > Options. A reset option restores only the toolbar without touching the ribbon. Customizations can be exported to a file and imported on another computer or by colleagues, but an import replaces all existing ribbon and toolbar customizations, so exporting first is advised. The page applies to Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Access, OneNote, Project, Publisher and Visio. Limits: button size cannot be changed, the toolbar cannot wrap onto several rows, and only commands can be added, not list values or individual styles.

recovery-time-objective.title: Architecture strategies for defining reliability targets – Azure Well-Architected Framework
recovery-time-objective.notes: This Well-Architected Framework page defines the recovery time objective as the longest period an application may be unavailable after an incident. The recovery point objective is the longest period of data loss that is acceptable during an incident. Both belong to the recovery targets, which express how effective business continuity and disaster recovery plans and tests are. Reliability targets fall into availability, correctness and recovery categories, and the page names MTTR and MTBF alongside RTO and RPO. The values are derived from failure mode analysis together with continuity and disaster recovery plans and tests. For each component, teams should define thresholds that trigger recovery, and those thresholds should allow for transient faults so recovery does not start too early. Platform guarantees must be considered, and Microsoft publishes RTO and RPO guarantees only for certain products. Targets have to be agreed with stakeholders and can change as workload complexity, customer count or technology changes. Workloads not properly tested against recovery metrics should not carry guaranteed SLAs. The page gives no universal numeric values.

risk-register.title: Assess cloud risks – Cloud Adoption Framework – Microsoft Learn
risk-register.notes: In the Cloud Adoption Framework, a risk register is a list of cloud risks holding all the information needed to identify, categorize, prioritize and manage them. It is built in the step of documenting cloud risks and then serves as the basis for deriving governance policies. The page recommends consistent wording so everyone understands the risks in the same way. Fields include a unique ID for traceability, an open or closed management status, a category such as security, cost or regulatory compliance, and a one-sentence description of the threat. Further fields cover probability, impact, and a priority that combines the two with a documented calculation method. Each entry also records a level, a management strategy of mitigate, accept, avoid or transfer, the concrete controls that enforce it, an owner with escalation path, and a closure date. The sample table shows risks such as unauthorized access to cloud services, mitigated with multifactor authentication and periodic access reviews. The register should be reviewed on a regular schedule and after events such as new technology or audits, and presented to the executive sponsor.

sec-rule-17a-4.title: SEC Rule 17a-4 – Microsoft Compliance
sec-rule-17a-4.notes: SEC Rule 17a-4 applies to securities broker-dealers and governs the electronic systems they use to keep records; a counterpart rule covers security-based swap dealers and major participants. Since the version effective in January 2023, a firm may satisfy the requirement in one of two ways. Option A is a complete, time-stamped audit trail recording all changes and deletions so the original can be recovered. Option B is storage in a non-rewriteable, non-erasable format, known as WORM. A third party that holds regulatory records must submit a signed undertaking to the SEC, and the firm must name a designated executive officer or independent third party to file it. Microsoft does not provide third-party undertaking services but describes a process for requesting an SEC undertaking letter through the admin center. Microsoft cites Azure immutable blob storage and preservation locks for WORM, and Microsoft Purview data lifecycle management, eDiscovery Premium and Audit Premium for the audit trail option. The page states that it is not legal advice and that compliance depends on correct customer configuration and remaining firm responsibilities.

security-orchestration-automation-and-re.title: Automation in Microsoft Sentinel: SOAR – Microsoft Learn
security-orchestration-automation-and-re.notes: This page presents Microsoft Sentinel as both a SIEM system and a platform for security orchestration, automation and response. The reason given is that security operations teams receive so many alerts and incidents that staff are overwhelmed, so alerts get ignored and incidents stay uninvestigated. Automation is meant to handle repetitive, predictable tasks in enrichment, response and remediation, freeing time for deeper investigation and threat hunting. Two building blocks are described. Automation rules centrally manage incident automation: they can assign playbooks, tag, assign or close incidents and alerts, apply one response across several analytics rules, create task lists for analysts and control the order of actions. Playbooks are collections of response and remediation actions with logic, built on Azure Logic Apps workflows, which integrate with internal and external systems and run automatically on alerts or incidents or manually on demand. When used in the Defender portal, some limits apply: certain triggers only act on Sentinel alerts, rule execution can be delayed, rapid changes to one incident may be batched into a single update, and manual playbook runs on alerts or entities are not supported there.

security-service-edge.title: What is Global Secure Access? – Microsoft Entra
security-service-edge.notes: Security service edge is described as a category of network security: an identity-aware, cloud-based network perimeter for people working from anywhere while apps and data move to the cloud. Microsoft's offering consists of Microsoft Entra Internet Access and Microsoft Entra Private Access, grouped as Global Secure Access and managed in the Microsoft Entra admin center. It builds on zero trust principles of least privilege, explicit verification and assuming breach, and works together with Defender for Cloud Apps as a cloud access security broker. Internet Access acts as an identity-based secure web gateway with web content filtering by category and by fully qualified domain name, universal Conditional Access for internet destinations and detailed traffic logs. Private Access provides zero trust network access to private resources without a traditional VPN, covering IP ranges, FQDNs and app-specific access for TCP and UDP. Users need Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2, and both products are part of the Microsoft Entra Suite or can be bought separately. Remote networks for branch connectivity need a minimum number of licenses. Several capabilities are still in preview, and the Microsoft traffic profile lacks some Internet Access features such as web filtering and TLS inspection.

self-healing-architecture.title: Design for self-healing – Azure Architecture Center
self-healing-architecture.notes: A self-healing application detects failures, responds appropriately and returns itself to a fully working state; the goal is high availability and resilience that supports the workload's availability targets. The page describes three steps: detect failures, handle them gracefully, and log and monitor them for operational insight. Measures include decoupled components that communicate asynchronously, retries for transient faults, health endpoints that report the state of a service and its dependencies, circuit breakers to fail fast, and bulkheads to isolate critical resources. It also names queue-based load leveling, failover to other instances or regions, compensating transactions instead of distributed ones, checkpoints for long-running work, graceful degradation, throttling of clients and leader election. Fault injection and chaos engineering, including Azure Chaos Studio, are recommended to test recovery. Availability zones support resilience within a region. Limits noted: multi-region failover raises cost and can reduce performance, failover of stateful stores may require handling eventual consistency, and retries or failover do not replace proper error handling, whose failure path must be tested deliberately.

session-border-controller.title: Plan Direct Routing – Microsoft Teams
session-border-controller.notes: In Teams Direct Routing, a session border controller is a customer-provided, supported device that links an organization's own telephony infrastructure to Microsoft Teams Phone. It allows the use of existing PSTN carriers, integration of third-party telephony systems and more control over voice infrastructure. The controller connects over SIP with TLS to the Microsoft SIP proxy through primary, secondary and tertiary connection points, with automatic failover. Media normally flows through Microsoft media processors, and media bypass is a separate planning option. The device may prioritize or restrict codecs such as SILK, G.711, G.722 and G.729. Prerequisites include a Microsoft-certified controller, at least one PSTN trunk, a publicly reachable IP address, an FQDN in a verified domain of the tenant with a public DNS record, and a public trusted certificate. Firewall rules must allow the Teams IP ranges. Typical scenarios are PSTN carriers, third-party PBXs, analog devices and contact centers. Limits: Microsoft may decline support for uncertified devices, support goes first through the device vendor, and media cannot be re-targeted during an active call.

software-bill-of-materials.title: microsoft/sbom-tool – GitHub
software-bill-of-materials.notes: This repository documents Microsoft's open-source SBOM tool, which produces software bills of materials for software artifacts of any variety. Output is compatible with SPDX 2.2 by default, and SPDX 3.0 can be selected; both versions can be validated with the tool. To build the inventory, the tool hashes the files of a drop directory and lists them in the files section of the SBOM. It also scans a build components path for project files such as csproj or package.json to detect packages and dependencies, using the Component Detection library, and fills in license information through the ClearlyDefined API. Each SBOM gets a unique namespace based on an organization-wide base URI. The commands cover generating an SBOM for a package name, version and supplier, validating it, and redacting file references. Integration into CI/CD is described for GitHub Actions and Azure DevOps pipelines, and the tool can be installed via WinGet, Homebrew, as a .NET tool, as a Docker image or as a NuGet package. Limits: redaction only works for SPDX 2.2 SBOMs, and detected components depend on the package formats Component Detection supports. The page does not give a general definition of the term.

sp-invoke-external-rest-endpoint.title: sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint (Transact-SQL) – Microsoft Learn
sp-invoke-external-rest-endpoint.notes: The system stored procedure sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint calls an HTTPS REST endpoint that is passed in as an input argument. It is available in SQL Server 2025, Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance and SQL database in Microsoft Fabric. Typical uses are calling Azure Functions, reading or writing blob files, sending messages to Event Hubs and calling Azure OpenAI, with managed identity or a database scoped credential for authentication. Parameters cover the URL, payload, headers, HTTP method (POST by default), timeout, credential, response output and retry count. A return value of zero means an HTTP 2xx status; otherwise the received status code is returned. Callers need the EXECUTE ANY EXTERNAL ENDPOINT permission, and on SQL Server 2025 and Managed Instance the feature is off until enabled through sp_configure. Limits include a payload ceiling, a cap on concurrent calls, HTTPS only, no automatic redirect following, and retries only for certain status codes. In Azure SQL Database and Managed Instance only a list of allowed Azure endpoints can be called directly; other targets must go through Azure API Management. The page warns that the procedure can send data to an external location.
